title: Dark Matter and Dark Energy: The Invisible Universe
executive_summary: Dark matter and dark energy together make up ~95% of the total mass-energy content of the Universe, while normal baryonic matter (stars, planets, gas, humans) accounts for only ~5%.
image_caption: Computer simulation of dark matter filaments forming the Cosmic Web.

key_sections.title: Evidence for Dark Matter
key_sections.content: Vera Rubin's galactic rotation curves showed that stars at the outer edges of spiral galaxies move at the same orbital speed as inner stars, proving galaxies are embedded in massive invisible dark matter halos.

key_sections.title: Dark Energy and Accelerated Expansion
key_sections.content: In 1998, observations of distant Type Ia supernovae revealed that the expansion of the Universe is accelerating rather than slowing down under gravity. Dark energy is the repulsive pressure driving this acceleration.

key_sections.title: WIMPs and Search Experiments
key_sections.content: Leading dark matter candidates include Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) and axions. Underground detectors and particle accelerators continue experiments to detect direct dark matter interactions.
